display.purpose: Opposing match totals at standard desktop height.

display-short.purpose: Match totals at widths at least 901px and heights at most 850px.

display-phone.purpose: Match totals at widths at most 520px.

headline.purpose: Uppercase Banzuke wordmark at standard desktop width.

side-title.purpose: Claude Code and Codex names above the large totals.

body.purpose: Room text and the base size for semibold play names.

label.purpose: Supporting clock labels, navigation, and builder information.

label-small.purpose: Play kinds, ages, English ranks, and compact secondary labels.

japanese-rank.purpose: Japanese sumo rank with an English label beneath.

join-control.purpose: Signed-out mobile joining link in the live header.

feed-control.purpose: Transparent feed pause/resume button with normal button line height.

shadows.name: selected-filter-line

motion.name: data-ease
motion.purpose: Rope position, ranking position, and ranking-track width changes.

motion.name: rope-position
motion.purpose: Slide the marker to Codex points divided by combined points.

motion.name: ranking-position
motion.purpose: Move stable-keyed rows into their new rank positions.

motion.name: ranking-track
motion.purpose: Update a stable score track relative to the current leading stable.

motion.name: count
motion.purpose: React requestAnimationFrame count toward the target; reduced motion shows the final value immediately.

motion.name: score-flash
motion.purpose: Identify the side of a newly received scoring event; suppressed with reduced motion.

motion.name: lead-change
motion.purpose: Duration of Lead changes after a change between non-tied leaders; suppressed with reduced motion.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: Live-status dot only; muted DEMO dot is still.

motion.name: commentary-scroll
motion.purpose: Two-copy loop. Hover, focus within, and explicit pause each stop motion and freeze visible text.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All room CSS motion stops. Commentary becomes one wrapping line, values remain current, and rank/rope positions remain meaningful.

narrative.overview:
Banzuke presents a code competition through the ordered ranks of a sumo banzuke and the legible numbers of a sports broadcast. Pine charcoal grounds, ivory text, and stable side colors keep the match readable. Condensed scores carry the largest weight; thin rules and compact controls support them without adding another visual event.

This system governs the room board at `app/page.tsx` and its broadcast component variants. Other routes and the standalone tug variant retain their existing legacy theme. Extend the room's color, type, state, and alignment rules when adding room features. Its current header, full-width match, ranking/feed split, and closing ticker are a page composition recorded in `.impeccable/surfaces/app-page-tsx.md`, not a required template for every new screen.
keyCharacteristics: Large condensed scores with tabular numerals.
Japanese Mincho ranks paired with plain Barlow UI text.
Ochre Claude identity and sage Codex identity across data views.
Flat fields, fine boundaries, and motion tied to changing data.
Truthful LIVE/DEMO status and visible access to joining.

rules.name: The Side identity Rule
rules.body: Keep Claude and Codex colors consistent across match totals, ranks, plays, and rope labels. Pair color with the side's name or accessible text.

rules.name: The Status truth Rule
rules.body: Use live red for an actual LIVE state. Synthetic data carries DEMO and Demo plays.

rules.name: The Numeric alignment Rule
rules.body: Keep changing numbers tabular and right-align ranking and play values. Large match totals use condensed type, while their labels use Barlow.

rules.name: The Flat fields Rule
rules.body: Use tonal contrast and rules for room grouping. Keep selected-state marks separate from structural depth.

dos: **Do** preserve side identity in text, marks, and numeric data.
**Do** use condensed tabular numbers for changing room scores and clocks.
**Do** pair Japanese ranks with readable English translations.
**Do** preserve visible focus, selected controls, and the feed's scroll access.
**Do** keep private work labeled `a private repo` in both plays and commentary.
**Do** provide current values and complete wrapping commentary when motion is reduced.
donts: **Don't** introduce another accent for the existing Claude or Codex identity.
**Don't** add texture, bevels, hard offset shadows, or gradient lettering to the flat room broadcast.
**Don't** turn the current room page composition into a template for unrelated routes.
**Don't** treat the legacy root palette, legacy type, or legacy glow effects as room tokens.
